L24: # Quasi-particles in weak perturbations of non-interacting quantum lattice systems
L25: 
L26: D.A.Yarotsky Note: Department of Mathematical Physics, University College Dublin, Ireland; e-mail: yarotsky@mail.ru Note: on leave from Institute for Information Transmission Problems, Moscow, Russia
L27: Abstract. We consider a general weak perturbation of a non-interacting quantum lattice system with a non-degenerate gapped ground state. We prove that the presence of isolated eigenvalues in the spectrum of the decoupled model leads to the existence of quasi-particles in the perturbed model. Also, a scattering theory for asymptotically free many-particle states is developed.
L28: ## 1 Introduction and results
L29: We consider a quantum system on a lattice, which is a weak perturbation of a non-interacting system with a non-degenerate gapped ground state. A rigorous perturbation theory for ground states in such models was developed in [【11†1】, 【12†5】, 【13†9】, 【14†10】, 【15†11】, 【16†16】, 【17†17】, 【18†23】, 【19†24】]. In particular, it is known that the weakly interacting model has a unique gapped ground state. In the present paper we establish a quasi-particle picture in the corresponding sector of the model.
L30: We prove that if there are isolated eigenvalues in the spectrum of the decoupled system, then the weakly interacting system has particle-like states which are obtained perturbatively from the eigenvectors of the decoupled system. We then show that the existence of a quasi-particle subspace leads to subspaces, describing scattering states of asymptotically free finite collections of quasi-particles.
L31: An explicit quasi-particle picture for quantum Ising model in a strong magnetic field was developed by Malyshev in [【20†14】] (see also [【21†13】, 【22†15】]). The existence of one-particle subspaces in more complicated quantum spin systems was later shown in [【23†3】, 【24†26】].
L32: All these results for quantum spin systems rely on a special ground state renormalization, which makes the Hamiltonian into a generator of a Markov stochastic process (see [【25†2】, 【26†12】, 【27†18】, 【28†19】, 【29†20】, 【30†8】, 【31†25】] for results on quasi-particles for Markov processes). It appears, however, that the interpretation of the renormalized system as a stochastic process limits the applicability of the method and is not actually necessary for the study of quasi-particles.
L33: Indeed, in the present paper we show that the quasi-particle picture can be established for a quite general class of quantum models within the $C^{*}$-algebraic framework.
L34: We give now precise definitions.
L35: 
L36: We consider a quantum “spin” system on the lattice ${\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$. Suppose that for each $x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$ there is a Hilbert space ${\mathcal{H}}_{x}$ (possibly infinite-dimensional) associated with this site. For the restriction to a finite volume $\Lambda\subset{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$ we will use the notation
L37:  | $${\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}:=\otimes_{x\in\Lambda}{\mathcal{H}}_{x}.$$  |
L38: 
L39: The (formal) Hamiltonian of the model consists of a non-interacting Hamiltonian and a perturbation:
L40: 
L41:  | $$H=H_{0}+\Phi.$$  |
L42: 
L43: Here $H_{0}$ is the free Hamiltonian:
L44: 
L45:  | $$H_{0}=\sum_{x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}h_{x}.$$  |
L46: 
L47: We assume that each $h_{x}$ is a non-negative self-adjoint, possibly unbounded operator on ${\mathcal{H}}_{x}$ with a non-degenerate ground state $\Omega_{x}\in{\mathcal{H}}_{x}$:
L48:  | $$h_{x}\Omega_{x}=0$$  |
L49: 
L50: and a spectral gap $\geq 1$:
L51: 
L52:  | $$h_{x}|_{{\mathcal{H}}_{x}\ominus\Omega_{x}}\geq{\bf 1}$$  |  | (1)
L53: (this is necessary and sufficient in order that the non-interacting Hamiltonian have a non-degenerate ground state and a spectral gap $\geq 1$; here and in the sequel we slightly abuse the notation by denoting the one-dimensional subspace spanned by $\Omega_{x}$ with the same symbol). In order to define the perturbation $\Phi$ we fix a finite subset $\Lambda_{0}\subset{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$ (range of the perturbation) and set
L54:  | $$\Phi=\sum_{x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}\phi_{x},$$  |  | (2)
L55: 
L56: where $\phi_{x}$ is a self-adjoint bounded operator on ${\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda_{0}+x}$ (here $\Lambda_{0}+x$ is a shift of $\Lambda_{0}$). We will assume that the perturbation is small in the sense that $\sup_{x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}\|\phi_{x}\|$ is finite and small enough.
L57: Under these assumptions the model has a unique infinite volume ground state with a spectral gap and an exponential decay of correlations . It can be obtained rigorously as the limit of finite volume ground states. Let $\Lambda\subset{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$ be a finite volume and $H_{\Lambda}$ the restriction of the Hamiltonian $H$ to $\Lambda$ with empty boundary conditions:
L58: 
L59:  | $$H_{\Lambda}:=H_{\Lambda,0}+\Phi_{\Lambda},$$  |
L60: 
L61: where
L62:  | $$H_{\Lambda,0}:=\sum_{x\in\Lambda}h_{x},\quad\Phi_{\Lambda}:=\sum_{x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}:\Lambda_{0}+x\subset\Lambda}\phi_{x}$$  |  | (3)
L63: (other boundary conditions can be used as well). Since $\Phi_{\Lambda}$ is bounded, $H_{\Lambda}$ is self-adjoint with $\,\mathrm{Dom}\,(H_{\Lambda})=\,\mathrm{Dom}\,(H_{\Lambda,0})$. The following theorem shows that the presence of a non-degenerate ground state and a perturbative spectral estimate hold uniformly for all finite volumes:
L64: ###### Theorem 1.
L65: 
L66: There exists a constant $c_{1}$, depending only on the perturbation range $\Lambda_{0}$, such that if $\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|<c_{1}$ then for any finite $\Lambda$ the Hamiltonian $H_{\Lambda}$ has a non-degenerate ground state $\Omega_{\Lambda}$:
L67: 
L68:  | $$H_{\Lambda}\Omega_{\Lambda}=E_{\Lambda}\Omega_{\Lambda},\quad H_{\Lambda}|_{{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}\ominus\Omega_{\Lambda}}>E_{\Lambda}{\bf 1},$$  |
L69: 
L70: where $E_{\Lambda}$ is the ground state energy. Moreover, let
L71:  | $$\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}:=H_{\Lambda}-E_{\Lambda}{\bf 1}$$  |
L72: 
L73: be the renormalized Hamiltonian. There exists a constant $c_{2}=c_{2}(\Lambda_{0})$ such that
L74: 
L75:  | $$\,\mathrm{Spec}\,(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda})\subset\bigcup_{a\in\,\mathrm{Spec}\,(H_{\Lambda,0})}\{z:|z-a|\leq c_{2}\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|a\}.$$  |  | (4)
L76: 
L77: In particular, this gives a lower bound for the gap between 0 and the rest of the spectrum:
L78:  | $$\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}|_{{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}\ominus\Omega_{\Lambda}}\geq(1-c_{2}\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|){\bf 1}.$$  |  | (5)
L79: Now the thermodynamic limit of the ground states can be performed; the limiting, infinite volume ground state is to be understood as a state ($\equiv$ normalized positive linear functional) on the algebra of local observables (see, e.g, [【32†4】]). Let $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\Lambda})$ be the algebra of bounded operators in ${\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}$ for any finite $\Lambda$, and
L80:  | $$\mathcal{A}_{\infty}:=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subset{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}},|\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\Lambda})$$  |
L81: 
L82: the full local algebra. Let $\Lambda\nearrow{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$ mean that $\Lambda$ converges to ${\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$ in the sense that it eventually contains any finite subset. Then
L83: ###### Theorem 2.
L84: 
L85: There exists the thermodynamic week^{∗}-limit $\omega_{\infty}$ of the finite volume ground states:
L86: 
L87:  | $$\langle A\Omega_{\Lambda},\Omega_{\Lambda}\rangle\xrightarrow{\Lambda\nearrow{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}\omega_{\infty}(A),\quad A\in\mathcal{A}_{\infty}.$$  |
L88: 
L89: Throughout the paper by $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ we denote various scalar products.
L90: Using appropriate definition of the infinite volume ground state, one can show that in our model it is unique: see [【19†24】].
L91: Having found the infinite volume ground state, we use the GNS construction to define in a conventional way the Hilbert space ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$, describing local excitations of this ground state. Precisely, we consider the GNS triple $({\mathcal{H}}_{\infty},\pi_{\infty},\Omega_{\infty})$ (Hilbert space, cyclic representation of $\mathcal{A}_{\infty}$ in ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$, and the cyclic vector), associated with the state $\omega_{\infty}$ so that
L92:  | $$\langle\pi_{\infty}(A)\Omega_{\infty},\Omega_{\infty}\rangle=\omega_{\infty}(A).$$  |
L93: 
L94: Next we define the infinite volume Hamiltonian $H_{\infty}$ on ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$ as an appropriate limit of $\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}$; it is convenient to use the (week) resolvent convergence, because resolvent expansions are very relevant for the perturbation theory.
L95: ###### Theorem 3.
L96: 
L97: There exists a (unique) self-adjoint operator $H_{\infty}$ on ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$, which is the weak resolvent limit of $\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}$ in the following sense: for any $A,B\in\mathcal{A}_{\infty}$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}$
L98:  | $$\langle(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}-z)^{-1}A\Omega_{\Lambda},B\Omega_{\Lambda}\rangle\xrightarrow{\Lambda\nearrow{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}\langle(H_{\infty}-z)^{-1}\pi_{\infty}(A)\Omega_{\infty},\pi_{\infty}(B)\Omega_{\infty}\rangle.$$  |  | (6)
L99: Moreover, $H_{\infty}\Omega_{\infty}=0$ and estimates (【33†4】),(【34†5】) hold with $\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda},{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda},\Omega_{\Lambda}$ replaced by $H_{\infty},{\mathcal{H}}_{\infty},\Omega_{\infty}$, and $\,\mathrm{Spec}\,(H_{\Lambda,0})$ replaced by
L100: 
L101:  | $$\,\mathrm{Spec}\,(H_{\infty,0}):=\Bigl\{\sum_{x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}a_{x}\Bigl|a_{x}\in\,\mathrm{Spec}\,(h_{x}),a_{x}\neq 0\text{ only for finitely many }x\Bigr\}.$$  |
L102: Theorems 1-3 have been proved in [【11†1】, 【14†10】, 【18†23】].
L103: We are now in a position to discuss the main topic of this paper, the quasi-particle excitations. In addition to the assumptions made above we assume now that the model is translationally invariant, i.e., ${\mathcal{H}}_{x},h_{x},\phi_{x},\Omega_{x}$ are translates of some ${\mathcal{H}},h,\phi,\Omega$.
L104: This implies that the ground state is translationally invariant and there is a representation of lattice shifts by unitary operators $U_{x}:{\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}\to{\mathcal{H}}_{\infty},x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$, commuting with the Hamiltonian $H_{\infty}$. Let $\mathbb{T}^{\nu}$ be the $\nu$-dimensional torus of quasi-momenta (we will identify $\mathbb{T}$ with the segment $[0,1]$) and consider the Hilbert space $L_{2}(\mathbb{T}^{\nu})$.
L105: We shall say that an invariant with respect to $H$ and $U_{x}$ subspace $\mathcal{G}\subset{\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$ is a one-particle subspace if there is a unitary $V:\mathcal{G}\to L_{2}(\mathbb{T}^{\nu})$ such that $VU_{x}V^{*}$ is the multiplication by $e^{2\pi i\langle x,\cdot\rangle}$ and $VH_{\infty}V^{*}$ the multiplication by some function $m(\cdot)$ (which is the energy-momentum relation of the quasi-particle).
L106: Equivalently, an invariant $\mathcal{G}$ is a one-particle subspace if there exists an orthonormal basis $\xi_{x},x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}},$ in $\mathcal{G}$ such that $U_{x}\xi_{y}=\xi_{x+y}$; the unitary $V$ is then given by
L107:  | $$V:\xi_{x}\mapsto e^{2\pi i\langle x,\cdot\rangle}.$$  |
L108: The natural situation in which one expects the presence of a one-particle subspace and which we will only deal with is when the non-interacting Hamiltonian $H_{\infty,0}$ has a spectrally isolated one-particle subspace and the perturbation is sufficiently small.
L109: We assume therefore now that the single-site Hamiltonian $h$ has an isolated non-degenerate eigenvalue $\mu$ and $\mu\notin\cup_{k>1}\{\mu_{1}+\ldots+\mu_{k}|\mu_{i}\in\,\mathrm{Spec}\,(h),\mu_{i}\neq 0\},$ so that $\mu$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $H_{\infty,0}$, corresponding to the one-particle subspace spanned by $w_{x}\otimes(\otimes_{y\neq x}\Omega_{y}),x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$, where $w$ is the eigenvector of $h$:
L110:  | $$hw=\mu w;$$  |
L111: 
L112: the function $m$ identically equals $\mu$ in this case. By Th.3 and (【33†4】), if $\|\phi\|$ is sufficiently small then the part of the spectrum of $H_{\infty}$, lying in the segment $[(1-c_{2}\|\phi\|)\mu,(1-c_{2}\|\phi\|)\mu]$, is separated by gaps from the rest of the spectrum. Let ${\mathcal{H}}_{1}$ be the spectral subspace of $H_{\infty}$, corresponding to this segment. Then
L113: ###### Theorem 4.
L114: 
L115: If $\|\phi\|$ is sufficiently small, then ${\mathcal{H}}_{1}$ is a one-particle subspace, and the corresponding energy-momentum relation $m$ is a real analytic function.
L116: The final result we discuss here concerns existence of asymptotically free many-particle scattering states. Let $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}({\mathcal{H}}_{1})$ be the symmetric Fock space obtained from the above one-particle subspace ${\mathcal{H}}_{1}$ and describing various finite collections of these quasi-particles (in fact, though the indistinguishability of the particles is essential, the particular form of statistics is not relevant for the result below).
L117: The free evolution of a finite collection of quasi-particles is governed by the Hamiltonian $H_{f}$, acting on $\mathcal{F}$ and defined as the second quantization of $H_{\infty}|_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}$. We will show that the initial Hilbert space ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$ contains invariant subspaces, describing asymptotically, in distant past or future, free collections of quasi-particles.
L118: We have to assume now that the energy momentum relation $m$ is non-constant, otherwise there is no scattering and the particle picture breaks down. Denote by $U_{f,x}:\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{F}$ the second quantization of the unitary lattice shifts $U_{x}|_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}$ in the one-particle subspace. Then
L119: ###### Theorem 5.
L120: 
L121: There exist isometric wave operators $W_{\pm}:\mathcal{F}\to{\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$ such that $\,\mathrm{Ran}\,(W_{\pm})$ are invariant subspaces of $H_{\infty},U_{x}$, and $H_{\infty}|_{{\rm Ran}(W_{\pm})}=W_{\pm}H_{f}W_{\pm}^{*}$, $U_{x}|_{{\rm Ran}(W_{\pm})}=W_{\pm}U_{f,x}W_{\pm}^{*}$.
L122: Our proofs of Theorems 4 and 5 closely follow the paper [【31†25】] and we will omit here some technical details. The proof of Theorem 4 is a modification of Malyshev-Minlos technique (see [【25†2】, 【23†3】, 【30†8】, 【26†12】, 【22†15】, 【27†18】, 【28†19】, 【29†20】, 【31†25】, 【24†26】]). The proof of Theorem 5 follows general ideas of scattering theory for quantum many-body systems.
L123: In [【20†14】], the scattering theory was based on the well-known construction of many-particle states given by Haag and Ruelle in the axiomatic quantum field theory [【35†6】, 【36†7】, 【37†22】]. Our exposition is closer to the spin wave scattering for the Heisenberg ferromagnet as presented in [【38†21】], section XI.14.
L124: ## 2 Preliminary results. Theorems 1-3
L125: All theorems stated above rely heavily on perturbative expansions for the ground state, one-particle states and the Hamiltonian. We begin by briefly reviewing the proofs of Ths.1-3 (see [【18†23】] for details). From now on we adopt for brevity the following convention. We will denote by $c$ and $\epsilon$ various (generally different in different formulas) positive constants, which do not depend on the volume $\Lambda$, though may depend on the interaction range $\Lambda_{0}$.
L126: We write $\epsilon$ if this constant can be chosen arbitrarily small by choosing $\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|$ small enough; on the other hand the constant $c$ is typically greater than 1 and does not depend on $\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|$.
L127: The ground state vector $\Omega_{\Lambda}$ of the Hamiltonian $H_{\Lambda}$ in a finite volume can be found using a suitable ansatz, reflecting smallness of correlations between distant spins.
L128: 
L129: For any $I\subset\Lambda$ set
L130: 
L131:  | $${\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}:=\otimes_{x\in I}{\mathcal{H}}_{x}^{\prime},\;\;\Omega_{I,0}:=\otimes_{x\in I}\Omega_{x}$$  |
L132: 
L133: (with ${\mathcal{H}}^{\prime}_{\emptyset}\equiv\mathbb{C}$). It follows that
L134:  | $${\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}\ominus\Omega_{\Lambda,0}=\bigoplus_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}\otimes\Omega_{\Lambda\setminus I,0}.$$  |  | (7)
L135: 
L136: We will typically denote vectors from ${\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}$ by $u_{I},v_{I}$, etc. For each $u_{I}\in{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}$ we introduce a “creation” (or “spin raising”) operator $\widehat{u}_{I}$ in ${\mathcal{H}}_{I}$ by
L137: 
L138:  | $$\widehat{u}_{I}v=\langle v,\Omega_{I,0}\rangle u_{I},\;\;\;v\in{\mathcal{H}}_{I}$$  |
L139: (with $\widehat{u}_{\emptyset}$ a scalar operator). A useful property of these operators is that for any $I$, $J$ and $u_{I},v_{J}$
L140: 
L141:  | $$\widehat{u}_{I}\widehat{v}_{J}=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}0&\text{ if }I\cap J\neq\emptyset,\\
L142: \widehat{u_{I}\otimes v_{J}}&\text{ if }I\cap J=\emptyset.\end{array}\right.$$  |
L143: In particular, they commute. For any $v\in{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}$ such that $\langle v,\Omega_{\Lambda,0}\rangle=1$ there exists a unique collection $\{v_{I}\in{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}\}_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}$ such that $\exp\bigl(\sum_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\bigr)\Omega_{\Lambda,0}=v$ (these $v_{I}$ can be obtained by truncation from components of $v$ appearing in the decomposition (【39†7】)).
L144: Let $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$ be the ground state vector of $H_{\Lambda}$ normalized so that $\langle\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda},\Omega_{\Lambda,0}\rangle=1$ (i.e., $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}:=\Omega_{\Lambda}/\langle\Omega_{\Lambda},\Omega_{\Lambda,0}\rangle$).
L145: Initially the non-degeneracy of the ground state and its non-orthogonality to $\Omega_{\Lambda,0}$ is clear from the usual finite-volume perturbation theory for sufficiently weak perturbations in each particular volume, and it can be shown that the estimate for the perturbation which ensures this property can actually be chosen uniform in the volume. Let $\{v^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{I}\in{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}\}_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}$ be the corresponding collection such that
L146:  | $$\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=\exp\bigl(\sum_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{I}\bigr)\Omega_{\Lambda,0}.$$  |
L147: ###### Lemma 1.
L148: 
L149: For any $\epsilon>0$, if $\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|$ is sufficiently small then
L150: 
L151:  | $$\max_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{I\subset\Lambda:x\in I}\|H_{I,0}v_{I}^{(\Lambda,gs)}\|\epsilon^{-(d_{I}+1)}\leq 1,$$  |  | (8)
L152: 
L153: where $d_{I}$ is the minimal length of a connected graph containing $I$.
L154: The idea of the proof is to rewrite the Schrödinger equation $H_{\Lambda}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=E_{\Lambda}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$ as a fixed point equation for a suitable (non-linear) mapping on the space of collections, which is then shown to be a contraction in the set specified by Eq.(【40†8】).
L155: 
L156: Having found the ground state $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$, it is convenient for the study of the operator $H_{\Lambda}$ to use for vectors $v\in{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}$ the expansion
L157:  | $$v=\sum_{I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}.$$  |  | (9)
L158: 
L159: For any $v$, there exists a unique collection such that (【41†9】) holds: indeed, if we introduce the operators $P_{\Lambda,I}:{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}\to{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}$ by
L160: 
L161:  | $$u=\sum_{I\subset\Lambda}(P_{\Lambda,I}u)\otimes\Omega_{\Lambda\setminus I,0},\quad\forall u\in{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda},$$  |
L162: 
L163: then
L164:  | $\displaystyle v_{K}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle P_{\Lambda,K}\sum_{J\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{J}\Omega_{\Lambda,0}$  |  | (10)
L165:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle P_{\Lambda,K}\exp\bigl(-\sum_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{I}\bigr)\sum_{J\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{J}\exp\bigl(\sum_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{I}\bigr)\Omega_{\Lambda,0}$  |
L166:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle P_{\Lambda,K}\exp\bigl(-\sum_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{I}\bigr)v.$  |
L167: Using expansion (【41†9】), we rewrite the renormalized Hamiltonian $\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}$ as
L168: 
L169:  | $$\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}=\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}+\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda},$$  |  | (11)
L170: 
L171: where $\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}$ is the “diagonal” part defined by
L172: 
L173:  | $$\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}.$$  |  | (12)
L174: 
L175: For the renormalized perturbation $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}$ we then have
L176:  | $\displaystyle\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}-\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0})\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L177:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}-\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L178:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle[\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}-\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L179:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle[H_{\Lambda,0},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}+[\Phi_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}-\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L180:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle[\Phi_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}.$  |
L181: It is convenient to write the operator $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}$ in the form
L182: 
L183:  | $$\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=\sum_{J\subset\Lambda}\widehat{(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$$  |  | (13)
L184: 
L185: with some $(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}\in{\mathcal{H}}^{\prime}_{J}$, thereby expanding the image vector as in (【41†9】). Using (【42†10】), we find that
L186:  | $\displaystyle(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle P_{\Lambda,J}\exp\bigl(-\sum_{\emptyset\neq K\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{K}\bigr)[\Phi_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L187:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle P_{\Lambda,J}\exp\bigl(-\sum_{\emptyset\neq K\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{K}\bigr)[\Phi_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\exp\bigl(\sum_{\emptyset\neq K\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{K}\bigr)\Omega_{\Lambda,0}.$  |
L188: Expanding this expression into a commutator series and using Lemma 1, one finds that
L189: 
L190:  | $$\sum_{J\subset\Lambda}\|(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}\|\epsilon^{-(d_{J;I}+1)}\leq c\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\||I|\|v_{I}\|,$$  |  | (14)
L191: where by $d_{J;I}$ we denote the minimal length of a graph connecting all sites in $J$ to some sites in $I$. In particular, this estimate shows that $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}$ is a relatively bounded, in some special sense, perturbation of $\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}$. Indeed, we introduce a new norm ${|\!|\!|}\cdot{|\!|\!|}$ in ${\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}$ by
L192:
